text:
sam: heads-up — AZ16 PSU/fan microcode update scheduled for Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Observed intermittent thermal spikes on 2 racks during lab run. planning a soft-drain (evacuate non-latency-critical jobs) + staggered node reboots. :warning:

lia: what's the blast radius? will hosted customers see errors or just higher latency?

sam: blast radius: ~8% of az capacity if we cordon an entire cohort at once. goal is to keep user-facing pools unaffected by draining non-prod and low-priority pools first. hosted API should route to other AZs automatically.

kyu: can we use the burst pool for short-term backfill? we have ~120 GPU-hours free in burst (eu & us pools). cost estimate ~ $1.2k for the window if fully used. finance tagged: @tess.

tess: acknowledged. tag me if you expect > $2k. can we reduce time to 90m?

sam: we think 2 hours safe for sequenced reboots (firmware + burn-in checks). can cut to 90m if we parallelize two cohorts but that increases risk.

lia: prefer safer path — keep 2h. downstream jobs should be rescheduled. will add note to ops status page and update automations.

infra-oncall: I'm going to schedule a canary across 6 nodes 01:30-02:00 UTC, then proceed cohort A 02:00-02:40, cohort B 02:40-03:20, cohort C 03:20-04:00. if canary shows >5% error rate, rollback plan triggers.

sam: rollback plan = abort remaining cohorts, reprovision from standby pools, and revert microcode if required. notify #incidents.

kyu: runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/ops/runbooks/az-fan-psu-microcode (paste below).

sam: quick checklist (will paste to runbook):
```
- notify GC and hosted API routing (pre-warm other AZs)
- canary 6 nodes, health checks 5 min
- drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
- reboot, apply microcode, run `nvtop` + telemetry validation
- uncordon after 20m stable metrics
```

lia: do we need customer comms? only customers on dedicated pools in AZ16 might see reduced capacity.

sam: yes — send targeted email to dedicated customers in AZ16 with option to move workloads. I'll draft a short message. @tess can you sign-off?

tess: send me draft. include expected window and mitigation (burst pool & cross-AZ routing).

deploy-bot: scheduled: canary job created (job-id: canary-az16-2025-01), cohort A job created (cohort-a-az16-2025-01).

kyu: monitoring hooks to watch: GPU temp tail, NIC retransmits, API 99th latency, token throughput. set alerts: GPU_temp>85C for 3m -> page.

infra-oncall: added alert `az16.thermal_spike` and will mute noise for scheduled window. keep critical pages on.

lia: any extra cost besides burst pool? expect small reprovisioning credits if we spin up extra instances. estimate +5% billing variance for window.

sam: final ask: folks on-call during window: @infra-oncall, @kyu, @sam. keep Slack thread pinned, use #incidents if >2% error.

tess: approved. :+1:

sam: ok, I'll post to #status and update runbook with exact cohort node lists. thanks all.
